ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.Self)` (Bloodletting.cs:22-25) == cost 0 / SKILL / COMMON / SELF. No keywords.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new HpLossVar(3m)` + `new EnergyVar(2)` (Bloodletting.cs:14-18) == both numbers, both declared. `_energy` is in `Card._MAGIC_ATTRS` (cards/base.py:185-189) so `magic_number` reports 2.

OnPlay.rationale: Order matches: `CreatureCmd.Damage(..., 3, Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, this)` (Bloodletting.cs:31) == `DamageCmd.deal(..., props=DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS)`, then `PlayerCmd.GainEnergy(DynamicVars.Energy.BaseValue, Owner)` (32) == `EnergyCmd.gain(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self._energy)`. The energy verb's own semantics (the sim runs `hooks.modify_energy_gain` first, cmds.py:553) belong to the PlayerCmd half of the creature_card_cmds seam. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (29) and VfxCmd.PlayOnCreatureCenter (30).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Energy.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Bloodletting.cs:37) == `self._energy += 1` (2 -> 3). The HP loss stays 3 when upgraded on both sides.

guards.what: the sim returns early on `if ctx.player.is_dead` between the HP loss and the energy gain (bloodletting.py:38-39)

Verified by the task reviewer against the C# and against the diff (no other behavior changed).
